messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: residual calculation
parts:
Hi Ken,
I'm looking at the function calculateResiduals.ProbeLevelModel and I'm
a little confused about how the calculations are done. It seems like
the intensities y and the estimated intensities yhat are on the
intensity scale. But then the residuals are y-yhat. Shouldn't the
residuals be: log2(y)-log2(yhat) or on the intensity scale: y/yhat?
Thanks,
Elizabeth

#the main parts of the code
calculateEps <- getCalculateResidualsFunction(this)
phi <- getData(paf, indices = cells, fields = "intensities")
$intensities[oinv] # probe affinities
y <- getData(df, indices = cells, fields = "intensities")
$intensities[oinv] #original intensities
theta <- getData(cef, indices = cells2, fields = "intensities")
$intensities #chip effect
theta <- rep(theta, times = unitGroupSizes)
yhat <- phi * theta #estimated intensities
eps <- calculateEps(y, yhat)

> getCalculateResidualsFunction.ProbeLevelModel
function (static, ...)
{
function(y, yhat) {
y - yhat
}
}

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] residual calculation
parts:
Hi,

see Section "Quality assessment of summarized data" on the group page;
how the residuals are calculated depends on what PLM you used. Yes,
for the log-additive model it is on the log scale.

In the code, this is taken care of by the
getCalculateResidualsFunction() method. The default implementation
for any ProbeLevelModel is to calculate the residuals as the
difference on the intensity scale, but subclasses such as RmaPlm
provide alternative implementations, e.g.
getCalculateResidualsFunction.RmaPlm(). The latter, as you found out,
calculates this as:

e = y/yhat

The rational for this is that 'e' is on the intensity scale, which
will give you:

log2(e) = log(y) - log(yhat)

as you expected. (Footnote: As all signals in aroma.affymetrix,
residuals, are always store on the intensity scale, because it more
generic than the log scale which is only defined for (0,Inf)).

In the group pages under "For Developers", there is a section on
reproducibility with a graph showing that the above calculations give
close to identical results as what you affyPLM() returns.

Cheers

Henrik
